x: SiteBoard Site reporting dashboard for the WP12 Pan Borneo Sabah Fasa 1B supervision team. It reads the daily Site Daily Photo Reports made in the SDR app and turns them into matrices, a structure board, a photo gallery and weekly / monthly reports.

How it works IOWs make the daily report in the SDR app and send the PDF. The report admin (the RE or an assigned ARE) saves the PDFs into a reports folder on his or her computer. Open SiteBoard in Chrome, Edge or Brave (folder access enabled), connect that folder, and the matrices and reports are built from it. Report files never leave your computer. This website holds the program code only.

Team guide One page for everyone who uses the dashboard.

1. Who does what IOWs make the Site Daily Photo Report in the SDR app every working day and send the PDF to the report admin. REs and AREs report as required. Report admin (the RE or an ARE assigned to the task) receives the PDFs and saves each one into the reports folder on his or her own computer. Nobody changes the files once saved. Each person who wants to use SiteBoard needs the report PDFs in a folder on his or her own computer. A shared Google Drive folder is planned for later; until then reports are passed on by the report admin.

2. Filing rules Keep the file name exactly as the SDR app creates it, e.g. WP12-CST-MAT-20261016-1_SDR.pdf . Never rename or edit the PDF. Save into the current month folder, e.g. 2026-10 . If unsure, drop the file anywhere in your reports folder and press Tidy folder in Report files . A corrected report is generated again in the app, with the next number ( -2 ). The old file stays. Folders starting with _ or . are ignored by the dashboard.

3. Opening the dashboard (every team member) Use Chrome, Edge or Brave on a computer . Phones can view but cannot connect a folder. In Brave , first open brave://flags/#file-system-access-api , set it to Enabled and relaunch (Brave turns folder access off by default). Keep the SDR PDFs in one folder on your computer (month sub-folders are fine). Open the SiteBoard link and press Connect reports folder . Choose that folder and press Allow . Keep the tab open: it checks the folder every 20 seconds. Next time, press Reconnect folder once.

x: 4. Daily routine for the report admin (RE or ARE) Check Overview and Submissions for days with no report. If no report was needed (office work, leave, off site), click the red ✕ and mark it no report needed ; it is then left out of the compliance count. Use Reminder message (Submissions) to remind IOWs on WhatsApp, or Share / save matrix… to send the matrix picture with a description. Review Observations : set each to Open, Monitoring or Closed and add a note. At week end and month end use Generate report .

5. Sharing settings with the team Project details, who must report daily, non-working days and observation follow-up are stored in your browser. In Settings press Save settings to folder ; the file siteboard-settings.json is written into your reports folder. Give a copy of that file to a teammate (put it in the root of his or her reports folder) and it is read automatically.

6. If something looks wrong Open Report files : it lists files that could not be read, mismatches and duplicates. A report shows “not received” but was sent? Check that the PDF is in your reports folder and press Rescan . Reports made by SDR v1.2.6 or later carry exact data inside the PDF; older ones are read from the page layout and may need a check.

7. Photos and structures Photos shows every photo. Filter by date, reporter, activity, structure, zone, chainage or text. Click a photo to enlarge it; use the arrow keys to move on. Prepare all thumbnails makes the gallery load instantly next time. Structures lists the bridges, culverts, junction culverts and RS walls with the last record, status and photos. See Structures and photos .

8. Map and map statistics Import the project's SDR setup.json in Settings . SiteBoard uses its chainage, zones and centreline automatically. WP12 is already built in as the safe default. A KMZ/KML in Map is optional. It is kept in this browser for the current workspace and can add ROW boundaries and points of interest, or provide an alignment when the setup has no centreline. Choose the reporting period at the top. Type a from/to chainage or press Drag range on map and drag along the alignment. Turn on 100 m coverage to see which sections have photographed items. Red rings identify GPS points more than 250 m from the chainage written in the report. Use Map statistics… for a shareable PNG/PDF
9. Today view Open Today first thing: who has reported, what was done, which structures were worked and the day's photos. It shows the latest report day if nothing has come in yet today.

Reports, comments and memos Generate report builds the PDF; download it as PDF or Word, or send it by WhatsApp. In Report files , open a report and press Open PDF to read the original, or Comment / send via WhatsApp . Messages & memo : send Monitoring, Observation, Action needed or Follow-up messages, design an internal memo (PDF plus WhatsApp announcement) and see what was sent.
Structures and photos

Structure board Lists the 4 bridges, 32 culverts, 13 junction culverts and 3 RS walls from the SDR setup.json , with state ( Active in the last 7 days, Recorded , No record ), last activity and status, number of records and photos. How a work item is matched to a structure Assigned by you (see below). Structure code written in the report (C12, JC3, B2, RSW1) – exact. Description and chainage when no code is written. SiteBoard reads the type (box or pipe), size, side and river name from the text, then picks the nearest structure of that type. The chainage limit is wide because drawing chainages are indicative and culverts are moved or offset on site: about 150 m for culverts, 100 m for juncti

Photo gallery Filter by date, reporter, activity category, structure, zone, chainage range and text, or show only items with remarks. The large view shows the details, a link to the report, a GPS link (reports from SDR v1.2.6+) and a download button.

Choose Weekly or Monthly and the period. Fill in the report number, prepared / checked names and the planned works. Choose the photos (or let SiteBoard pick) and press Build report . Sharing the matrix and overview On Submissions press Share / save matrix… ; on Overview press Share / save overview… . A preview image is made for the period chosen at the top of the page. Share matrix + map… opens the Map and combines the matrix with the current map view and filters. The description is written for you (period, compliance, who has no report on which days) and can be edited. Choose Send via WhatsApp , Download image (PNG), Download PDF or Copy image . On a computer WhatsApp cannot receive the image from a web page: SiteBoard downloads it and opens WhatsApp, and you attach it with the paperclip (or paste it if you used Copy image ).

Opening, commenting and sending In Report files , click a report reference, then Open PDF to read the original SDR PDF in a browser tab straight from your folder. Comment / send via WhatsApp (same panel), the Comment… button on each item and Send… in Observations open the message composer with the details filled in. Messages & memo holds the composer for Monitoring, Observation, Action needed, Follow-up and General messages, the internal memo designer, and a record of what was sent. On a phone the file goes straight into WhatsApp. On a computer WhatsApp cannot receive a file from a web page, so SiteBoard downloads the file and opens WhatsApp; attach it with the paperclip.
Administrator notes

Editing these notes The pages are written in Markdown in docs-src/ . After editing, run pip install -r tools/requirements-docs.txt and then python3 tools/build_docs.py to rebuild docs/ ; commit both folders. The pinned documentation dependency makes the build repeatable. The notes use the same design as the SDR app documentation.

Adding people Anyone with the link can open SiteBoard, but it only shows reports from a folder on that person's own computer. To let an ARE act as report admin, give him or her the PDFs (and a copy of siteboard-settings.json ). A shared Google Drive folder is planned for later.

Another work package Create or switch to a workspace for that package, connect its reports folder, import that package's SDR setup.json , check the project details, and Save settings to folder . The import validates and applies the chainage limits, zones, sections, centreline, structures and activity mappings together. Nothing in the code needs to change. An incomplete or invalid setup is rejected and the current project remains active.

Categories and wording The WP12 SDR setup (version 7: 52 structures, 193 activities) is built in, so existing workspaces work without importing anything. Exact SDR activity names decide the category; anything not in the list falls back to the keyword rules in js/config.js . After a project's SDR setup changes, use Settings → Import SDR setup.json. Settings shows the active range and the number of zones, structures and centreline points.

Ecosystem and wider use

The two apps The SDR app is the capture tool: one person, one day, one PDF with photos, chainage, activity, BQ, structure, RFI and GPS. SiteBoard is the monitoring tool: it reads every SDR PDF and shows the whole team and the whole project. Everything SiteBoard shows starts as an SDR report. Can the contractor use it? Yes, with the same code. It only needs a folder of SDR-format PDFs, so a contractor team that produces SDR reports can connect its own folder and get the same matrices, structure board, gallery and period reports. Points to settle first: - Keep the folders separate. The consultant's supervision records and the contractor's own records are different documents with different purposes. Each organisation connects its own folder and keeps its own settings file. - Team filter. Two sensible routes, smallest first: 1. Snapshot page (recommended first step). SiteBoard exports one self-contained HTML page with the period's numbers and charts (reporting compliance, works by category, progress by zone, structure status, rain days, RFIs) and optionally selected photos.
